exposure: Fissurectomy and anoplasty with V-Y cutaneous advancement flap
cohort: 30 patients affected by chronic anal fissure (CAPF) without hypertonic internal anal sphincter (IAS).
finding: Fissurectomy and anoplasty resulted in all patients healing within 40 days, no de novo post-operative anal incontinence cases, and only two recurrences within 18 months that healed after conservative therapy, showing good results at 2 years after surgery.
